clue.text: See 11
Hunter — one preparing breakfast?

definitions.meaning: someone who hunts game illegally on another's land
a cook who simmers eggs out of their shells for the morning meal

explanation.definitionFit: A poacher is both an illegal hunter of game and, playfully, a cook who poaches eggs.

clue.text: Find new home for plant, climbing and lush

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to transfer a plant into a new pot is to repot it

explanation.surface: A gardener moving a plant to a new pot, with the plant climbing and growing lush.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is a heavy drinker, as is a toper, an old word for a habitual boozer.

clue.text: Possible lark ending in coarse ribaldry, -unfortunately

indicators.note: the ending of the word coarse means its last letter is taken
the word ribaldry is unfortunately mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lark of a joke ended in coarse, unfortunate bawdiness.
explanation.walkthrough: A lark is the bird, but here it stands as the classic example of a person who rises at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is the standard example of someone who gets up early, the opposite of a night owl.

clue.text: Tipple offered as Batman finally snared by the Riddler?

indicators.note: something snared by another is caught inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to riddle is to sieve, so a riddler is a sifter

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Batman

explanation.surface: Batman, caught at last by his foe the Riddler, is offered a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riddler is Batman's comic-book enemy, but here a riddle is a coarse sieve, so the riddler is a SIFTER, which takes in N.
explanation.definitionFit: A snifter is a small drink of spirits, a synonym of tipple.

clue.text: In Bayeux, where threading hole is weaving

indicators.note: the French word threads through the hole, going inside it

parts.note: a sinus is a cavity or hollow, as in the skull
in French, spoken in Bayeux, the word for where is ou

explanation.surface: A question about the Bayeux Tapestry: where the threading goes through a hole as it is woven.
explanation.walkthrough: Bayeux is a French town (home of the tapestry), signalling a French word: ou, 'where'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sinuous winds and twists, the way a weaving road or river does.

clue.text: Steep incline misjudged badly under expedition's leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A steep slope was badly misjudged by the leaders of an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective for the slope, but it is a verb: to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it thoroughly, and to imbue is to saturate or permeate it.

clue.text: Change menu — tart's off

indicators.note: the words are off, meaning out of order, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its s as a letter: tarts

explanation.surface: A restaurant changes its menu because the tart has gone off or is no longer served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges MENU and TARTS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute is to change one form or substance into another, as alchemists hoped to do with lead.

clue.text: They scrape together artist, king, queen and son

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: An artist, king, queen and son gather together in a royal portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakers are people who rake, drawing leaves or soil together by scraping.

clue.text: On which cap forms the gap

indicators.note: the letters of the words form something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cap fitting into a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat peg is a hook on which one hangs a cap or other headgear.

clue.text: Relate called for a sexy participation in torture

indicators.note: one piece takes part within another, sitting inside it

parts.note: torture causes pain
pert means saucy or attractively perky

explanation.surface: A demand for some sexy role-play in a torture scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called for' is only a link joining the definition to the wordplay; 'participation in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain to something is to relate or belong to it.

clue.text: See 15
13's creation — trouble with author

parts.note: to harry someone is to harass or trouble them
Beatrix Potter was the author of Peter Rabbit

explanation.surface: A writer's character who brings trouble along with an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is J K Rowling, so her creation is her boy wizard; the author here is a different writer, Beatrix Potter.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy wizard is the most famous character created by the author at 13 across.

clue.text: 13's creation — for flipping eternal youth's a boy in the money

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other

parts.note: a fee is money paid

indicators.note: the pieces are flipped, so read backwards

parts.note: Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up, is the eternal youth: hence Pan's
Ross is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A creation of the author, explained with eternal youth and a boy in the money.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Pan is the boy who never grew up; the 'a' before 'boy' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The potions master at Hogwarts is a character created by the author at 13 across.

clue.text: Successful author's ___ in it, you might say!

definitions.text: Successful author's ___ in it, you might say!

parts.words: Successful author's ___ in it, you might say!
parts.note: a successful writer is rolling in it, i.e. very rich, and the author's surname sounds like the missing word

explanation.definitionFit: J K Rowling is a hugely successful author, and her name sounds like rolling, as in rolling in money.

clue.text: Seaside features line up above poles, about a -hundred

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the first piece over the next
in a down clue, up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a row is a line

indicators.note: the poles go about, around, the hundred

parts.note: masts are poles on ships
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Lining up above flagpoles on a seafront, about a hundred of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Worm casts are the coiled heaps lugworms leave on sandy beaches, hence seaside features.
explanation.definitionFit: Worm casts are the coiled heaps of sand left by lugworms on beaches, typical seaside sights.

clue.text: 13's creation — star seemingly eclipsed?

parts.note: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky
an eclipsed object looks dark, black

explanation.surface: A star that has seemingly been eclipsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry's godfather is a character created by the author at 13 across.

clue.text: Field where lyricist has fit

parts.note: Tim Rice is a famous lyricist of musicals
a paddy is a fit of temper, informal British usage

explanation.surface: A field where a lyricist throws a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice paddy is a flooded field where rice is grown.

clue.text: Businessman on speed regressing

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: re means on, concerning
to dart is to move at speed

explanation.surface: A businessman on speed whose habits are regressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressing' turns both pieces round together, so 'on speed' reads backwards as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods, a kind of businessman.

clue.text: Not entirely Blue Period that takes a grilling?

parts.note: a blue steak is barely cooked; one not quite that raw is rare
a bit is a period of time, as in 'wait a bit'

explanation.surface: Not quite Picasso's Blue Period, but something put under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blue Period is Picasso's; blue in steak terms means nearly raw, so not entirely blue is RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, cooked under the grill.

clue.text: American subject accepts British award for unmentionable work?

indicators.note: the subject accepts, takes in, the award

parts.note: Americans call mathematics math, not maths
the CBE is Commander of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An American subject accepting a British honour for a scandalous piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors superstitiously avoid naming Shakespeare's Scottish play in a theatre, so it is the unmentionable work.

clue.text: See 25
Attend to layer protecting English vessel of old

indicators.note: the layer goes round, protecting, the other pieces

parts.note: a hen is an egg layer
Noah's ark is the ancient vessel

explanation.surface: Seeing to a layer of protection on an old English ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A layer looks like a coating but is a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearken is to listen, an old-fashioned way of saying attend to.

clue.text: 13's creation — witch free

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A witch set free in a writer's creation.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-giant gamekeeper of Hogwarts is a character created by the author at 13 across.

clue.text: An essential pole switched, then handed down

indicators.note: one pole letter, N for north, is switched for the other, S for south

parts.note: central means essential, key

explanation.surface: An essential pole being switched and then handed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole switched' changes the N of CENTRAL to S: CESTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancestral is inherited, handed down from forebears.

clue.text: See 12
Stages where charity work taken over

indicators.note: taken over, turned, means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: aid is charity
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Stages where a charity's work has been taken over.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia are raised platforms, plural of podium, so stages.

clue.text: 13's creation — life oddly requiring oxygen following state of unconsciousness in cart

indicators.note: the pieces go in the cart

parts.note: a dray is a cart

indicators.note: the next pieces come after, following, the first

parts.note: a coma is a state of unconsciousness

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of life are taken

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A life in a cart, oddly needing oxygen after a coma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring' is a link; the dray is a low flat cart once used by brewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry's school rival is a character created by the author at 13 across.

clue.text: He's 10 and dreads his part for a start

indicators.note: his part is a portion of the following words, the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A black actor in dreadlocks, describing his part for a start.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is the second word of the godfather's name. A Rastafarian is typically of African descent and wears dreadlocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafarians, often of African heritage, characteristically wear their hair in dreadlocks.

clue.text: Accounts here in the red?

parts.note: a bank where accounts are held in red stuff: donations of blood

explanation.definitionFit: A blood bank stores donated blood, red deposits, the way a bank holds accounts.

clue.text: Take a scalpel to the cult from hell?

indicators.note: the cult comes from, after, hell

parts.note: Dis is the underworld in classical myth
a sect is a cult

explanation.surface: Taking a scalpel to the cult from hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect is to cut apart, as one does with a scalpel.

clue.text: Conclusion of capitalist that secures business for mogul

indicators.note: the conclusion of the word is its last letter
one piece secures, holds, another inside

parts.note: yon is a dialect word for that
Co is short for company

explanation.surface: The capitalist ending up securing business as a mogul.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy and powerful magnate, a mogul.
